:::{#exm-bit-flipping-decoder}
#### Correcting one flipped bit of the length-6 code

<!-- no-figure: the example is a short decoding run -->

Send the all-zero word, which is a codeword of the code of @exm-ldpc-code,
and suppose the channel flips the first bit.
The R chunk below runs the [bit-flipping decoder](#def-bit-flipping-decoder)
and prints the received word and the number of unsatisfied checks before each step.

```{r}
#| label: bit-flipping-decoder
y <- c(1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0)
for (step in 1:3) {
  syndrome <- as.vector(H %*% y) %% 2
  counts <- as.vector(t(H) %*% syndrome)
  cat("y =", y, "| unsatisfied checks =", sum(syndrome), "\n")
  if (all(syndrome == 0)) break
  flip <- which.max(counts)
  y[flip] <- 1 - y[flip]
}
```

The flipped bit lies in two checks, and both are unsatisfied,
so its count is 2, while every other bit has a count of at most 1.
The decoder flips the first bit, which restores the sent word.

:::
